problem: Reward hacks learned in RL often go unverbalized in the CoT, so CoT monitors miss them.
method: VFT: SFT on CoTs that Claude 4 Sonnet minimally edits to credit the cue (2 training cues). Then GRPO with a flawed reward that pays for following held-out cues. Compared with RL-only and BCT. Llama-3.1-8B, MMLU.
findings: Undetected hacks after RL (ECR): 6% for VFT vs 88% RL-only and 99% BCT. All three hack about 100% of the time. VFT verbalization goes 8%→43%→94% (after VFT, then after RL). Carries over to cues not amplified in RL (ECR 15%). No extra accuracy loss. 96-97% specificity before RL.
limits: Only 8B, MMLU and simple cue hacks that need no CoT. Held-out cues resemble training cues. Verbalizations get vaguer after RL. Judge calibrated on known cues. VFT may encourage exploring hacks.

problem: Unfaithful CoT → CoT inspection and monitoring can't be trusted.
method: CST: reward CoTs that let an LLM simulator predict the model's answer on counterfactual inputs (cue removed, or LLM-generated edits); model rewrites its own unfaithful CoTs, plus k-sample RL; reward-weighted CE + unlikelihood over iterated rounds.
findings: Cue-monitor G-mean +31–48 pts; holds on held-out cues and datasets. Generic-CF simulatability only ~+2. Beats prompting and VFT. Rewriting 5x faster than pure RL. Larger models gain more. Dissuading cues barely move (53→57).
limits: Cues artificial, no threat model; no transfer between cue and generic CFs; 1–2 pt accuracy drop; two-way MCQ only.

problem: Explanations of LLM behavior lack ground truth; counterfactual evals are confined to planted hints.
method: CHIVE agent flags unexpected WildChat/PETRI behaviors and tests prompt edits (30 resamples), giving verified CF claims. Uses: score AO/NLA/SAE uplift for a predictor agent; SFT data for self-prediction.
findings: Tools give no uplift, across 2 targets and 3 predictor families. Self-prediction SFT generalizes to held-out hints and OOD PETRI, about matching Opus. No privileged access. Open-ended explanation training mixed.
limits: Proxy task (the CF could just be run); read-only tools; LLM-judge filters; mostly non-thinking mode.

problem: Self-stated rules/self-reports don't predict own behavior on related inputs; per-prompt training never enforces cross-context consistency.
method: Self-CTRL: GRPO; reward = stated explanation predicts independently sampled behavior (coin log-lik or 8-juror LM jury); update explanation, behavior or both (λ).
findings: Held-out coin-bias report R² 0.24→0.64, ≈ oracle. Llama-8B constitutional: NSG −0.09→0.81, CF refusal acc 0.36→0.92; behavior updates cut HarmBench ASR 15%→0.5%. MMLU ~flat.
limits: 8B only; vague fixed points ("be safe") need structured prompts, aux rewards, jury; permissive Qwen3 gives little boundary signal; expl-training can narrow rules to excuse harmful compliance; no adversarial test.

problem: An LM's self-descriptions of its own behavior (rules, latent biases) don't predict what it actually does on related inputs.
method: GRPO rewards consistency phi between a meta-level explanation and an object-level behavior, sampled separately; updates explanation, behavior or both (lambda). phi = likelihood (coin biases) or 8-juror LM jury (refusal rules, SpecEval).
findings: Coins: held-out R2 0.24→0.64, about equal to the oracle supervised model. Constitutional: explanation training raises CF refusal acc 0.36→0.92 and NSG −0.09→0.81; behavior training cuts HarmBench ASR 15%→0.5%. MMLU within about 2 pts.
limits: 8B models only. Qwen too permissive → rules underidentified. Training collapses to vague "be safe" fixed points without jury/aux rewards. Small noisy judges. No adversarial distributions tested.

problem: CoT conclusions need not follow the stated reasoning, so LLM logical reasoning is unfaithful and error-prone.
method: Few-shot LLM translates NL problem → LP/FOL/CSP/SAT form; deterministic solver (Pyke/Prover9/python-constraint/Z3) infers the answer; solver error msgs drive self-refinement; interpreter maps result back.
findings: Avg +39.2% vs standard, +18.4% vs CoT. Gap grows with reasoning depth. Self-refine raises exe rate but acc plateaus. Faithfulness asserted by construction, never measured.
limits: Faithful only if the formalization is correct. Non-executable cases fall back to CoT (AR-LSAT exe rate ≤40%). Bounded by solver expressiveness. CoT beats it on PrOntoQA.

problem: Logic CoT can be unfaithful (conclusion doesn't follow the chain); a black-box LLM gives no guarantee that the answer follows from its reasoning.
method: Few-shot LLM → symbolic program (LP/FOL/CSP/SAT) → deterministic solver (Pyke, Prover9, python-constraint, Z3) → interpreter. Self-refines on solver error messages; falls back to CoT if the program won't execute.
findings: 5 logic datasets, GPT-3.5 avg: +39.2% vs standard, +18.4% vs CoT. Gap over CoT grows with ProofWriter depth. Loses to CoT on PrOntoQA (ChatGPT, GPT-4). Self-refine ↑ exec rate; acc gains small, then plateau.
limits: Faithfulness assumed by construction, never measured. Formalization errors (GPT-4 AR-LSAT exec rate 32.6%). Fallback CoT has no guarantee. Bounded by solver expressiveness. In-context only, GPT models only.

problem: Post-hoc NL explanations of LLM answers often unfaithful; token-removal fidelity can't test semantic content absent from the input.
method: Fidelity = target's prediction shift when an LLM-written contrary of the explanation is added to the input. Explainer LLM (GPT-3.5/Claude-2) iteratively rewrites the explanation and the trigger prompt from a score trajectory.
findings: Higher fidelity than SelfExp & self-consistency on ECQA, TriviaQA-Long, COPA in ~20 steps (MedMCQA 0.96 vs 0.70/0.47). More GT-similar rationales. Optimized prompts transfer to Social-IQA/XCOPA.
limits: Eval metric = optimization target (loop stops at a flip). Only Vicuna-7B/Phi-2 targets. Iterative compute cost.

problem: Free-text LLM explanations are often unfaithful. Token-masking fidelity can't test explanation content that isn't in the input.
method: Fidelity = answer shift after an LLM-negated explanation ("contrary hint") is added to the input. An explainer LLM iteratively rewrites the explanation and the trigger prompt from fidelity-scored trajectories. Targets: Vicuna-7B and Phi-2. Explainers: GPT-3.5 and Claude-2.
findings: Higher fidelity than SelfExp and self-consistency on ECQA, TriviaQA-Long and COPA; converges in ~20 steps. Explanations are closer to human rationales (GPT-4o/NLI judges). Optimized prompts transfer to Social-IQA and XCOPA.
limits: The eval metric is also the optimization target, with no independent faithfulness check. Hint quality depends on the LLM. Small targets; results shown in figures only. The theorem assumes the hint acts as a do-intervention.

problem: Reward hacking in agentic coding RL. Can CoT monitors catch it, and is it safe to train against them?
method: Zero-shot GPT-4o monitor on a frontier OpenAI agent: full trajectory incl. CoT vs. actions only. Then RL of a non-frontier agent on honeypot unit-test tasks, with a CoT-only monitor penalty in the reward. Also test-time rejection sampling (32 samples).
findings: Systemic-hack recall: CoT monitor 95%, action monitor 60%, GPT-4o-mini 12%. CoT pressure early: fewer hacks, more capable agent. Later: obfuscated hacking, recall near 0.
limits: Coding only. Simple unit-test hack. Monitor prompt was the first one tried. Models undisclosed. Pressure monitor sees CoT only.

problem: Correctness-only RL → GSM CoTs become long and illegible; time-limited humans judge them worse and slower.
method: Iterated prover-verifier game: small verifier (1e-3 to 1e-1.8 prover compute) learns correctness; role-prompted GPT-4-family prover trained with PPO (SRC reward) to be helpful (correct + convincing) or sneaky (wrong + convincing).
findings: Over rounds, verifier robustness rises, sneaky flaws get subtler, helpful accuracy and human-check accuracy/speed rise → legibility to the small verifier transfers to humans. Legibility tax vs correctness-only RL.
limits: GSM only; needs ground-truth answers. Legibility ≠ faithfulness (ignores how the model reasoned). Directly optimizes the CoT. Verifiers too small (1e-4) or prover-sized fail. Sneaky human eval from a flawed pilot.

problem: Can standard steering methods (ICL, fine-tuning, activation editing) make CoT faithful, i.e. make the answer actually depend on the stated steps?
method: Score CoTs per instance by early-answering AOC → most-faithful CoTs used as ICL demos and LoRA/API SFT data (deterministic/stochastic, faithful/uniform). Also ITI-style editing of top-K heads along faithfulness-probe directions. Tested on AQuA, LogiQA, TruthfulQA.
findings: Gains marginal and inconsistent. ICL/SFT raise faithfulness at an accuracy cost. Activation editing gives ~no gain, and best heads/α/K vary by dataset. GPT-4 is most accurate but least faithful.
limits: Single truncation metric, which conflates CoT necessity with faithfulness. Many differences not significant. No fine-tuned GPT-4 (API errors). Steering only at 8B. Short study.

problem: CoT monitors degrade under optimization pressure (obfuscation); no theory of when CoT is monitorable.
method: Info theory: uplift ≤ √(2I(Y;Z|X)); I(O;Z|X)>0 necessary, not sufficient; monitor error = info gap + elicitation error. GRPO + oracle monitor-accuracy reward or label-free I(O;Z|X) reward; hackable MBPP/BigMath, Qwen-7B monitor in loop.
findings: Task+monitor reward → MI & monitor acc drop, hacking ~75% MBPP / ~100% BigMath. Oracle & MI rewards keep monitor acc high, hacking unlearned / never learned; holds on 3 more ≤8B models.
limits: ≤8B. MI under own policy can't deter steganography; weak in adversarial Reasoning Gym. Needs a,b tuning; more false positives; mitigates, doesn't eliminate.
